messages.subject: blavaan 0.3-7 is released
messages.body_plain: blavaan 0.3-7 went on CRAN at the end of last week. It now uses the future package for post-MCMC parallelization (which will also work on Windows, unlike before) and includes some other bug fixes. A new bug has already been identified involving blavInspect(,"lvmeans") for target="stan", which is already fixed in the github version.

messages.subject: Factor scores from blavInspect()
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I found a discrepancy regarding factor score estimates derived from the lavPredict() and blavInspect() functions.

The estimates of factor scores from lavPredict() using outputs from lavaan and blavaan are very similar. However, they have poor correlations with the posterior mean of factor scores obtained from blavInspect() using the output of blavaan. We used the latest version of lavaan and the GitHub version of blavaan.

# Package versions
packageVersion('blavaan')
0.3.8.513
packageVersion('lavaan')
0.6.5

Below is an illustrative example after some modifications to the example code in the blavaan GitHub website:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/blob/master/tests/blavaan_examples.R

rm(list=ls())

library(blavaan)

library(lavaan)

HS.model <- 'visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3

textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6 '

# Model fitting

fitblavaan<- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
                          burnin=1000, sample=1000, target="stan",
                         save.lvs=TRUE, n.chains=2)

fitlavaan <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)

# blavInspect() applied to the blavaan object

bfs <- blavInspect(fitblavaan,"lvmeans")

# lavPredict() applied to the blavaan object

bfs_lavPredict <- lavPredict(fitblavaan,"lv")

# lavPredict() applied to the lavaan object

fs_lavPredict <- lavPredict(fitlavaan, type = "lv")

head(bfs)
head(bfs_lavPredict)
head(fs_lavPredict)

cor(bfs[,1], bfs_lavPredict[,1])
cor(bfs_lavPredict[,1], fs_lavPredict[,1])
cor(bfs[,1], fs_lavPredict[,1])

#----------------- Results-----------------#

head(bfs)

           visual       textual
[1,] -0.9904806 -0.1398672

[2,] -0.6457269 -1.9026200

[3,] -0.4945887 -0.1356137

[4,] -1.2416560 0.6750524

[5,] -0.3828767 0.4183933

[6,] -0.8448696 -0.7858671

head(bfs_lavPredict)

            visual       textual
[1,] -1.00000645 -0.15394226

[2,] -0.09521353 -1.03934284

[3,] -0.68790500 -1.85575251

[4,] 0.55511171 0.02832575

[5,] -0.51631324 -0.13373992

[6,] -0.15099515 -1.36233917

head(fs_lavPredict)

             visual         textual
[1,] -0.8904454 -0.15265788

[2,] -0.1063254 -1.03766873

[3,] -0.6430584 -1.85423553

[4,] 0.5162538 0.03224754

[5,] -0.4853933 -0.13364084

[6,] -0.1606221 -1.36026125

#--------- Correlations----------#
cor(bfs[,1], bfs_lavPredict[,1])
0.1031521

cor(bfs_lavPredict[,1], fs_lavPredict[,1])
0.9997841

cor(bfs[,1], fs_lavPredict[,1])
0.1034387

Kind regards
Mehdi Momen

messages.subject: blavaan terminates normally but not posterior results
messages.subject_clean: blavaan terminates normally but not posterior results
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I am running blavaan with target="jags".  I am using 1000 adaptation steps, 5000 burnin and 100000 post-burnin iterations.  The sample size is 51 and it is a relatively simply growth curve model.  The model terminates normally, but I am not getting any posterior results, not even the column labeling for the posterior mean, sd., etc.  I am currently running the same model with target="stan" but it is taking a very long time.  Any thoughts would be appreciated.

Thanks

David

messages.subject_clean: blavaan terminates normally but not posterior results
messages.body_plain:
David

Is this showing the start of the summary, but  doesnt show the posterior results? Like showing this
> summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)
lavaan 0.6-5 ended normally after 35 iterations

  Estimator                                         ML
  Optimization method                           NLMINB
  Number of free parameters                         21

  Number of observations                           301

This has happened to me when the R session is calling the summary method from lavaan instead of blavaan. My solution has been to restart the R session and be sure to load first lavaan and the blavaan, so that R calls first the summary of blavaan

Also, if this is the case, your blavaan object has all the results shouldnt be neccesary to run it again, and it can have the same issue with either jags or stan

messages.subject_clean: blavaan terminates normally but not posterior results
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

In addition to what Mauricio said, one other possible fix might
involve the priors. Try adding the argument

dp = dpriors(itheta='dgamma(1,.5)', ipsi='dgamma(1,.5)', target='jags')

to your bgrowth/bsem/bcfa command. The priors associated with
variances are a bit in flux right now, and the gammas above (on
precisions) might work better for some models than the current
default.

Best,
Ed
